title: 1% better every day: what's a year worth?
description: 1.01 and 0.99 to the 365th power: compounding explained in charts.

shots.title: 1.01 vs 0.99: the question
shots.say: 1% a day sounds tiny. But what happens if you keep it up, or let it slip, for a whole year?

shots.title: 1.01 to the 365th: the curve climbs to 37.78
shots.say: Multiply by 1.01 every day. You have doubled by day 70, and after a year you are at about 37.78.

shots.title: 0.99 to the 365th: the curve sinks to 0.026
shots.say: Now take 0.99 every day. Half is gone by day 69, and a year later only about 2.6% is left.

shots.title: Both on a log scale: about 1,480 times apart
shots.say: On a log scale, both become straight lines. After a year, one is about 1,481 times the other.

shots.title: The caveat: a year of small habits
shots.say: Of course, nobody improves by exactly 1% a day. What really compounds is a small habit, kept up day after day.

shots.title: End card
shots.say: So don't wait for one big day. Show up every day.
